story.text: 해가 지고 나니 산성시장 골목에 불빛이 하나둘 켜졌습니다. 노포 치킨집 앞, 우리는 나란히 자리를 잡았습니다.
story.reading: hae-ga ji-go na-ni san-seong-si-jang gol-mog-e bul-bit-i ha-na-dul kyeo-jyeot-seum-ni-da. no-po chi-kin-jib ap, u-ri-neun na-ran-hi ja-ri-reul jab-at-seum-ni-da.
story.en: Once the sun went down, the lights came on one by one along the alleys of Sanseong Market. In front of an old-school chicken restaurant, we took our seats side by side.

story.text: "오늘은 '치맥'이 딱입니다." 메뉴판을 넘기는 손이 유독 신나 보였다고, 친구가 웃으며 놀렸습니다.
story.reading: "o-neul-eun 'chi-maek'-i ttag-im-ni-da." me-nyu-pan-eul neom-gi-neun son-i yu-dok sin-na bo-yeot-da-go, chin-gu-ga us-eu-myeo nol-lyeot-seum-ni-da.
story.en: "Today calls for exactly this — 'chimaek'." My friend teased that my hand flipping through the menu looked unusually excited.

story.text: 양념 반, 후라이드 반이 나오고, 잔이 부딪혔습니다. "'건배'." 격식은 여기서도 빠지지 않았습니다.
story.reading: yang-nyeom ban, hu-ra-i-deu ban-i na-o-go, jan-i bu-dich-yeot-seum-ni-da. "'geon-bae'." gyeok-sig-eun yeo-gi-seo-do ppa-ji-ji an-at-seum-ni-da.
story.en: Half seasoned, half fried arrived, and our glasses clinked together. "'Cheers'." Even here, my formality never quite left me.

story.text: "기장님은 치킨 먹을 때도 꼭 격식을 차리네." 친구의 놀림에, 저는 젓가락 대신 손으로 치킨을 집으며 웃었습니다. 그래도 '안주'는 역시 치킨이 최고입니다.
story.reading: "gi-jang-nim-eun chi-kin meog-eul ttae-do kkok gyeok-sig-eul cha-ri-ne." chin-gu-ui nol-lim-e, jeo-neun jeot-ga-rak dae-sin son-eu-ro chi-kin-eul jib-eu-myeo us-eot-seum-ni-da. geu-rae-do 'an-ju'-neun yeok-si chi-kin-i choe-go-im-ni-da.
story.en: "Even eating chicken, you still keep up appearances, Captain." At my friend's teasing, I laughed and picked up the chicken with my hands instead of chopsticks. Still, chicken really is the best 'drinking snack'.

story.text: 빈 접시가 금세 늘어났습니다. "여기, 반 마리만 더 '시켜'도 될까요?" 제 목소리는 이미 신이 나 있었습니다.
story.reading: bin jeop-si-ga geum-se neul-eo-nat-seum-ni-da. "yeo-gi, ban ma-ri-man deo 'si-kyeo'-do doel-kka-yo?" je mok-so-ri-neun i-mi sin-i na iss-eot-seum-ni-da.
story.en: The empty plates piled up fast. "Excuse me, could we 'order' half a chicken more?" My voice already had a bounce of excitement in it.

story.text: "이 집, 우리 '단골' 하자." 취기가 살짝 오른 채로 그렇게 말하고 나니, 어쩐지 든든한 약속처럼 느껴졌습니다.
story.reading: "i jip, u-ri 'dan-gol' ha-ja." chwi-gi-ga sal-jjak o-reun chae-ro geu-reo-ke mal-ha-go na-ni, eo-jjeon-ji deun-deun-han yak-sog-cheo-reom neu-kkyeot-seum-ni-da.
story.en: "Let's make this place our 'regular spot'." Saying that with a light buzz on, it somehow felt like a reassuring promise.

story.text: 치킨 두 마리와 맥주 몇 잔이 비워질 때까지, 우리는 웃음을 멈추지 못했습니다. 그날 밤 나눈 대화를 들려드리겠습니다.
story.reading: chi-kin du ma-ri-wa maek-ju myeot jan-i bi-wo-jil ttae-kka-ji, u-ri-neun us-eum-eul meom-chu-ji mot-haess-seum-ni-da. geu-nal bam na-nun dae-hwa-reul deul-lyeo-deu-ri-get-seum-ni-da.
story.en: Until two whole chickens and several glasses of beer were finished, we couldn't stop laughing. Let me share the conversation we had that night.

words.example_en: Friday nights, chimaek is the truth (the best choice).
We raised our glasses and toasted.
There's no side dish like chicken for drinking.
This place is our regular spot.

sentences.en: Friday nights, chimaek really is the best.

sentences.ko: 치킨은 맥주와 가장 잘 어울리는 안주입니다.
sentences.reading: chi-kin-eun maek-ju-wa ga-jang jal eo-ul-li-neun an-ju-im-ni-da
sentences.en: Chicken is the drinking snack that pairs best with beer.
I was hungry so I ordered one more.
This chicken restaurant became our regular spot.

turns.speaker: 상우
turns.text: 메뉴가 다양한데, 양념과 후라이드 중 어느 쪽으로 시킬까요?
turns.reading: me-nyu-ga da-yang-han-de, yang-nyeom-gwa hu-ra-i-deu jung eo-neu jjog-eu-ro si-kil-kka-yo?
turns.en: There are so many options — should we order seasoned or fried?

turns.speaker: 승객
turns.text: 반반 시키자. 그래야 둘 다 먹지.
turns.reading: ban-ban si-ki-ja. geu-rae-ya dul da meok-ji.
turns.en: Let's order half-and-half. That way we can have both.

turns.speaker: 상우
turns.text: 합리적인 판단입니다. 그럼 맥주도 첫 잔은 제가 사겠습니다.
turns.reading: hab-li-jeog-in pan-dan-im-ni-da. geu-reom maek-ju-do cheot jan-eun je-ga sa-get-seum-ni-da.
turns.en: A rational decision. Then I'll buy the first round of beer.

turns.speaker: 승객
turns.en: You're so reliable, as always. Come on, let's toast first!

dialogues.question: 두 사람이 치킨을 주문한 방식은 무엇인가요?
dialogues.question_en: How did the two of them order their chicken?
dialogues.explanation: 승객의 제안에 따라 두 사람은 양념과 후라이드를 반반씩 시켜서 둘 다 맛볼 수 있게 했습니다.

turns.speaker: 승객
turns.text: 야, 근데 너 술 취하니까 목소리 진짜 부드러워진다?
turns.reading: ya, geun-de neo sul chwi-ha-ni-kka mok-so-ri jin-jja bu-deu-reo-wo-jin-da?
turns.en: Hey, but your voice gets seriously softer when you're a little drunk, you know?

turns.speaker: 상우
turns.en: ...Is that so? Even a control tower has to rest sometimes.

turns.speaker: 승객
turns.text: 이 집, 우리 단골 하자. 다음에도 여기서 치맥 하는 거야.
turns.reading: i jib, u-ri dan-gol ha-ja. da-eum-e-do yeo-gi-seo chi-maek ha-neun geo-ya.
turns.en: Let's make this our regular spot. Next time too, let's do chimaek here.

turns.speaker: 상우
turns.en: Sounds good. That promise, I'll make sure to keep it.

dialogues.question: 두 사람이 이 치킨집에 대해 어떤 약속을 했나요?
dialogues.question_en: What promise did the two of them make about this chicken restaurant?
dialogues.correct_answer: 이곳을 둘의 단골집으로 삼고 다음에 또 오기로 했다
options: 이곳을 둘의 단골집으로 삼고 다음에 또 오기로 했다
dialogues.explanation: 승객이 이 가게를 둘의 단골집으로 삼자고 제안했고, 상우는 다음에도 함께 오겠다고 약속했습니다.
